AUDIO TRANSCRIPT
ERA V
Dr. Mara Vey
Continuity Archive Statement. I want the wording exact. Containment did not fail when EP-7 escaped a laboratory. Containment became impossible years earlier.
We distributed it. I helped design an organism that could survive transport. VCF sold it as food security. Governments stockpiled it. Relief agencies carried it across borders.
Families kept growth kits. Military shelters stored dormant cultures. Orbital stations grew it above the planet. We are searching for the moment the organism crossed the perimeter.
There wasn't one. There was a commercial rollout. Every strategy based on restoring the original boundary is attempting to restore something that never existed.

AUDIO TRANSCRIPT
ERA VIII
Dr. Lena Orlov
If this archive survives, then Continuity has outlived its purpose. We failed to preserve this civilization. We saved people. Families. Hospitals for another week.
A shelter for another month. A town through another winter. Those things mattered. But the system is ending. This archive is no longer an emergency briefing. It is a warning to whoever builds next.
Do not misunderstand us. We were not surrounded by fools. We were surrounded by institutions solving immediate problems with tools that genuinely worked in the short term.
Civilization can destroy itself without anyone choosing destruction. Remember that. Especially when your machines begin working well.

AUDIO TRANSCRIPT
ERA VIII
Dr. Sora Kel
Continuity Site North is operational. Barely. We're simplifying everything. No polymers where metal works. No complex system where a simple one survives.
Mechanical controls where electronics are unnecessary. Gravity feed instead of pumps. Ceramic storage. Replaceable seals accessible without dismantling half the machine.
I spent my career making civilization more advanced. Now I'm trying to make what remains harder to kill. Maybe sophistication without maintainability was one of our blind spots.
There are settlements north of here still functioning. Small ones. Less infrastructure. Less substrate. Fewer systems to fail. I think the future, if there is one, may begin smaller than we expected.

AUDIO TRANSCRIPT
ERA VIII
Dr. Mara Vey
We chose the name Continuity because at the beginning we thought that's what we were protecting: government, food, medicine, power, civilization.

Now I think the word means something else. Not preserving everything unchanged. Nothing survives unchanged. Maybe continuity means carrying enough forward that the next people don't have to begin from zero.
A seed. A machine. A medical text. A warning. An archive. A memory. If you're hearing this, then something continued.
Maybe not us. Maybe not Meridian. Maybe not the world we knew. But something. That will have to be enough.
